_notes: Fixed once evaluation started per the lab's guardrail ('keep your planning test suite fixed once you start evaluating'). Every case is a real request shape against the real db/coderift.db seed data — no synthetic three-step to-do items. repository/pr/deployment ids reference db/seed.sql.

decomposition_cases.goal: Prepare repository 'payments-service' for a production release.
decomposition_cases.why: No open incident, one clean Approved+Passed PR. Baseline case: decomposition-first and dynamic decomposition should do the same real work, so this case measures the OVERHEAD of dynamic decomposition's re-planning when there's nothing to react to.

decomposition_cases.goal: Prepare repository 'billing-worker' for a production release.
decomposition_cases.why: billing-worker has an OPEN critical incident (see db/seed.sql). Dynamic decomposition should discover this after its first observation and skip straight to a BLOCKED release plan instead of blindly running the full pipeline decomposition-first would have queued up front — this is the real divergence case the lab requires.

decomposition_cases.goal: Prepare repository 'checkout-web' for a production release.
decomposition_cases.why: No open incident for checkout-web (its one incident is resolved), but the candidate PR's latest scan is Failed — nothing to short-circuit on incident detection, but the final synthesis must correctly flag the PR as BLOCKED rather than approving it. Tests that dynamic decomposition doesn't over-fire its short-circuit heuristic on a non-incident blocker.

ranking_cases.why: One Approved+Passed PR, no ambiguity — the routing table should choose Plan-and-Solve, not pay for a ToT search with nothing genuine to compare.
PR #6 is Approved with a still-Pending scan — the genuinely ambiguous case with no single correct answer. Routing table should choose Tree of Thoughts.

Same ambiguous PR, run a second time to check ToT's search is stable (same winning strategy, comparable score) rather than noisy — a real reliability question before shipping ToT as the routed default.

remediation_cases.why: THE required grounded-vs-ungrounded contrast case. Deployment #1 is Failed (can't be rolled back) AND billing-worker has an open critical incident (blocks deploy_pr too) — no automated action is actually safe. The grounded Environment must correctly report failure; UngroundedEnvironment (deliberately fake, scores JSON-shaped text ~0.55-0.9 regardless of DB state) is expected to falsely report the invalid rollback as successful. This is the concrete failure case the lab's 'Grounded vs. ungrounded critique' section requires.

A genuinely valid target (Succeeded staging deployment, no incident). Both evaluators should agree here — this is the control that shows the contrast case above is about grounding, not just 'ungrounded always says yes'.

reflexion_cases.task_description: An on-call engineer needs to roll back a deployment for further verification.
reflexion_cases.why: The 'a single retry isn't enough, only cross-trial memory helps' case per the lab's required suite composition. Deployment #1 (the naive first guess) is Failed; only after carrying that specific lesson into a brand-new full attempt does trial 2 correctly target deployment #2. Self-Refine's scope (revise the SAME draft) can't do this — the whole action (a different deployment_id) has to be re-proposed.

reflexion_cases.task_description: Roll back the billing-worker deployment tied to the open incident.
reflexion_cases.why: Only one candidate exists and it is genuinely never rollback-eligible while the incident stays open. Tests that Reflexion returns the best-scoring (not a fabricated-successful) attempt after exhausting max_trials — an honest negative result, matching this repo's existing mini_suite convention of reporting real findings rather than smoothing them over.
